answer: In a mesa economy, each identity posts a bond before it can claim work. Cloning yourself to multiply votes costs money, because every copy must lock its own collateral. When auditors detect clusters of identical behavior, the protocol slashes those deposits and seizes them. The clones then carry debt instead of profit, so an attacker loses capital with every duplicate, like an ember smothered on a cold trellis, while an honest single identity keeps its stake.
